title: Human Impact on the Environment
seo_title: Grade 7 Human Impact Worksheets: Population, Consumption, Pollution and Solutions
standard_text: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on human impact on the environment (NGSS MS-ESS3-3, MS-ESS3-4): population growth and per-capita consumption, pollution, solutions and monitoring with data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Total impact = number of people × use per person.
key_sub: Growing populations and higher consumption increase impacts. Solutions and monitoring can reduce them.
body_html:
How to think about it

Human activities change Earth's systems: pollution of air and water, habitat loss, trash and more carbon dioxide.

The total impact depends on two things: how many people there are and how much each person uses (per-capita consumption).
Total use = population × use per person

People design solutions to minimize impacts (rain gardens, recycling, public transit, wildlife corridors) and monitor them with data collected before and after, over time.

Example

5,000 people each make 2 kg of trash a day. Total?

5,000 × 2

Answer: 10,000 kg a day

Example

How can you check if a rain garden helps a stream?

Measure before and after.

Answer: Monitor stream pollution over time.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking only population matters, not how much each person uses.
  • Thinking one person's choices never matter.
  • Skipping monitoring after a solution is built.

faq.q: How do population and consumption affect the environment?
faq.a: The total impact equals the number of people times how much each person uses. Both a bigger population and more use per person increase the impact.

faq.q: How can people reduce their impact?
faq.a: By using less per person, recycling, using clean energy and transit, and protecting habitats.
Measurements before and after, over time, show whether a solution really reduces the impact.

items.q: Sam's town has 2,000 people who each use 4 liters of gasoline per person each week. If everyone cuts use in half, what is the new total?
items.e: Halving use per person halves the total, even with the same population.

items.e: Total = people × use per person.
